claim_verdicts.evidence: Domain csproj uses Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk", no references (claim 2). ASP.NET Core docs: "Projects that target the `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` SDK implicitly reference the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App` framework." SDK errors: NETSDK1086 FrameworkReference "is implicitly referenced by the .NET SDK" (Microsoft.NETCore.App). EF Core / Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL are NuGet packages, absent here; missing reference -> CS0246 (claim 4).

True as written: ProductsController(DonHangDbContext db) runs `db.Products...ToListAsync()`/`FindAsync`; OrdersController.Get/List call `repository.FindAsync`/`ListByCustomerAsync` (IOrderRepository -> EfOrderRepository via AddScoped in ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:15); DonHang.Api.csproj references DonHang.Infrastructure. But the lesson lists these as the shortcuts, and AuthController(DonHangDbContext db) also queries `db.Customers.FirstOrDefaultAsync(...)` directly.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: The split is not perfectly clean: the products and login endpoints in `DonHang.Api` query `DonHangDbContext` directly, and the read endpoints for orders call the data layer without going through `OrderService` — shortcuts a later lesson in this module comes back to.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Dtos.cs:9 `public sealed record OrderDto(int Id, int CustomerId, string Status, DateTimeOffset PlacedAt, List<OrderItemDto> Items);` — no name field; OrdersController.ToDto builds it. FindAsync includes only Items. So adding the name to the GET response needs the Include in EfOrderRepository plus OrderDto/ToDto in DonHang.Api. Change 2 needs no HTTP change: ExceptionHandlingMiddleware already maps ArgumentException to 400.

issues.text: Fill blank is ambiguous given the lesson text: section 5 says `DonHang.Api` 'holds the HTTP side', `DonHang.Domain` 'holds the business side', `DonHang.Infrastructure` 'holds the data side', and the projects are 'one per kind of concern'. 'side' and 'concern' both fit the blank and are rejected by the answer set.
issues.quote: `DonHang.Api`, `DonHang.Domain` and `DonHang.Infrastructure` each hold one ____ of the API.
issues.fix: Reword so only 'layer' fits, e.g. en: "In Đơn Hàng, each of `DonHang.Api`, `DonHang.Domain` and `DonHang.Infrastructure` is one ____ — the lesson's word for a group of classes that change for one kind of reason." (vi tương ứng). Keep answers layer/tầng/tang.

issues.text: The list of shortcuts omits the login endpoint: AuthController (DonHang.Api) injects DonHangDbContext and runs `db.Customers.FirstOrDefaultAsync(c => c.Email == request.Email)`. A reader who opens the repo will find a third bypass the lesson presents as absent.
issues.quote: the products endpoints in `DonHang.Api` query `DonHangDbContext` directly
issues.fix: Replace with 'the products and login endpoints in `DonHang.Api` query `DonHangDbContext` directly'; update claim 12 to add 'AuthController.Login queries DonHangDbContext.Customers directly (AuthController.cs:11-16)'.

issues.text: The lesson body no longer says 'architecture', but the q1 question still does ('layered architecture' / 'Kiến trúc phân tầng'). 'Architecture' is not in known_vocab or Core concepts, so the round-1 unknown term is back in the quiz.
issues.quote: What does a layered architecture group classes by?
issues.fix: Reword en to 'When an application is split into layers, what are its classes grouped by?' and vi to 'Khi chia ứng dụng thành các tầng, các class được nhóm theo tiêu chí nào?'.

issues.text: The lesson replaced 'driver' with 'the Npgsql package that lets EF Core talk to PostgreSQL', but the q5 correct explanation (en and vi) still says 'the PostgreSQL driver' / 'driver PostgreSQL'. 'Driver' is not in known_vocab or Core concepts.
issues.quote: so the business layer cannot use EF Core, the PostgreSQL driver or ASP.NET Core types.
issues.fix: Replace 'the PostgreSQL driver' with 'the Npgsql package' in en, and 'driver PostgreSQL' with 'package Npgsql' in vi.

issues.text: The q4 context still says 'HTTP interface' (vi 'giao diện HTTP'). The lesson now uses 'interface' only for C# interfaces (IOrderRepository, INotifier), so this second sense made me stop.

issues.fix: Replace 'no HTTP interface' with 'no HTTP endpoints' (vi: 'không có endpoint HTTP').

issues.text: Options b ('more layers are always better') and c ('five projects, to be ready for any future need') are obviously wrong; d is the only other choice. The answer can be picked by wording without understanding.
issues.quote: Split it into five projects, to be ready for any future need.
issues.fix: Replace c with a plausible distractor, e.g. 'Split it into two projects, one for reading the CSV and one for computing the total, so each has one reason to change.'

issues.text: Option d ('layers only exist in large companies') is still something no reader would pick, so q2 is effectively a choice among three.
issues.quote: False, because layers only exist in large companies.
issues.fix: Replace d with a plausible wrong reason, e.g. 'False, because each layer must live in its own Git repository.' (vi tương ứng).
